What if time started moving backward?
Not in a laboratory.
Everywhere at once.
It starts with small things you almost don't notice.
Rain lifts off the pavement… and climbs back into the storm.
Spilled coffee flows up the table, back into the cup.
A shattered glass pulls itself together on the kitchen floor.
In Tokyo, it is nine at night.
Cars glide backwards down the expressway.
In New York, it is breakfast.
Steam falls back into the street.
In Cape Town, birds fly tail-first over the harbour.
Nobody is hurt.
Nothing is broken.
Everything is simply going back.
And nobody on Earth can stop it.
Then.
Every river turns around in its bed.
After one hour, the sea pulls back and does not return.
Ships lean over in the empty air where the water used to be.
After one day, every tree takes its leaves back.
Petals climb off the grass, back onto the flowers.
After one week, broken buildings rise back into shape.
Concrete and glass fly upwards, and the dust goes with them.
After one month, the cities go dark.
Eight billion people, moving backwards through their own lives.
After one year, the deserts take back the fields.
Sand moves uphill, and swallows the fences.
After ten years, everything we built is coming apart.
Towers come apart, floor by floor.
After a hundred years, the planet is what it was before us.
Forests cover the roads.
Towers stand in the trees.
Then comes the worst part.
Nothing new can ever happen again.
Every fire burns backwards.
Every meal uncooks itself.
Every chain of events runs backwards, step by step.
There is nothing left to look forward to.
But here's the twist.
Time was never one single river.
In orbit, satellites already live in a slightly faster time.
Their clocks gain about thirty-eight microseconds every day.
And it already happened to a man.
Sergei Krikalev spent eight hundred and three days in orbit.
He came home two hundredths of a second younger than the rest of us.
That is real time travel.
We just cannot feel it.
So… if time really started going backwards… which day would you live again?
